Hi Irene — thanks for the recap and the materials. Quick answers from procurement POV: 

- Procurement default is PO and vendor onboarding for anything recurring or > $5k per month. They require a completed W9 and supplier questionnaire; I’ve cc'd procurement so they can confirm the exact form set.
- Marketplace would be ideal because our internal process is much lighter for marketplace transactions (we can provision subscriptions quickly), but it depends on whether Redwood is listed on our marketplace vendor catalogue.

Procurement team — can you confirm the W9 + questionnaire we need and whether MegaData can accept a marketplace vendor relationship (or if Redwood needs to be onboarded)?

Aditya / Irene — adding finance perspective / AP policy specifics so procurement has clear expectations: 

- Vendor onboarding: once we receive a completed W9 + supplier questionnaire, typical internal processing time is 8–12 business days; exceptions can be requested but not guaranteed.
- PO vs Card thresholds: our policy allows P-card (corporate card) use for software purchases up to $10,000 one-time; recurring contracts generally require PO if committed spend > $5,000/month.
- Marketplace purchases: if Redwood is a marketplace partner that invoices through the marketplace, our AP can treat it as a SaaS subscription with a faster approval path (often 1–3 business days). Please confirm marketplace partner status.
- Temporary workaround: approve a 3-month pilot via P-card or marketplace to start immediately, then convert to PO for longer-term commitments. If procurement needs a formal credit hold, we can issue an invoice net-30 but that still requires vendor onboarding for tax/compliance.

Attachment: vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx — checklist we need from procurement (W9, remit address, primary contact, SOC2 attestation if required).
